These are words describing a basic commercial transaction involving a buyer and a seller exchanging money and goods, taking the perspective of the buyer. The words vary individually in the patterns of frame element realization they allow. For example, the typical pattern for the verb BUY: BUYER buys GOODS from SELLER for MONEY. Abby bought a car from Robin for $5,000.
The Buyer wants the Goods and offers Money to a Seller in exchange for them.
The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.
The means by which a commercial transaction occurs.
Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction.
In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods.
The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer.
This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The Reason for which an event occurs.

Any description of the purchasing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Buyerthat affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The individual intended by the Buyer to receive the Goods.
The length of time from when the commerce event began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The Buyer's intended purpose for the Goods.

These are words describing basic commercial transactions involving a buyer and a seller exchanging money and goods, taking the perspective of the seller. The words vary individually in the patterns of frame element realization they allow. For example, the typical patterns for SELL: SELLER sells GOODS to BUYER for MONEY. Robin sold a car to Abby for $5,000.
The Buyer has the Money and wants the Goods.
The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.
The means by which a commercial transaction occurs.
Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction.
In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods.
The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer.
This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The Reason for which an event occurs.

Any description of the selling event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Seller that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The state of the Seller after the sale has occurred.
The length of time from when the commerce event began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The Buyer's intended purpose for the Goods.
This FE indicates that the selling act reverses an earlier separate act in which the current Seller bought the Goods from the current Buyer.
This FE indicates that the selling act constitues a re-selling by the current Seller of Goods that they bought earlier from a third person who is not the Buyer of the current selling act.

A Recipient starts off without the Theme in their possession, and then comes to possess it. Although the Source from which the Theme came is logically necessary, the Recipient and its changing relationship to the Theme is profiled. I got two whistles from John.
The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The Theme is the object that changes possession.
The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied. Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.
The Place denotes where the Getting takes place.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The Reason refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.
The Means is the action of the Recipient which results in their possession of the Theme.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally acts.
The state that either the Recipient or the Theme end up in after the acquisition.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The Beneficiary is an entity which the Recipient passes the Theme to, or shares the Theme with.

Water in some solid or liquid form (the Precipitation) falls from the sky at a particular Place and Time, lasting for a particular Duration. The Rate or Quantity of precipitation may also be indicated.
The water in liquid or solid form that falls from the sky is the Precipitation.
The Quantity of Precipitation that falls within a certain Duration.
The Quantity is the amount of Precipitation that has fallen in a precipitation event or events. It is usually measured as the height that the Precipitation attains if prevented from further movement.
The amount of time for which the precipitation event lasts.
The Cause is the reason for the precipitation event.
The way in which the precipitation falls.
This FE identifies the temperature of the precipitation.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

Ambient conditions of temperature, precipitation, windiness, and sunniness pertain at a certain Place and Time. Further Specification of the conditions that pertain may also be indicated. A blustery storm blew in. There was a thick blizzard last night. An armada of hailstorms swept through the region.
This FE identifies the Place where the weather occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the weather occurs.
This FE identifies a further Specification of the weather conditions.
